name: West Texas and northern Mexico, Apr-Jul 2011
why: April-July 2011: 22,578 harmonized hotspots in this box vs a typical 1,954 for the same months, 1,155% of the 2003-2022 median. Across the whole region the peak month was 562% of median. Texas's record 2011 drought fire season.

name: Northern New Mexico (Texas region box), May 2022
why: May 2022: 3,011 harmonized hotspots in this box vs a typical 4 for the same months, 86,025% of the 2003-2022 median (this area normally has almost no fire then). Across the whole region the peak month was 505% of median. The box is the Sangre de Cristo mountains, where the Hermits Peak / Calf Canyon fire burned in spring 2022.

name: Rondonia / Bolivia border, Nov-Dec 2023
why: November-December 2023: 7,707 harmonized hotspots in this box vs a typical 144 for the same months, 5,348% of the 2003-2022 median. Across the whole region the peak month was 353% of median. Late-season burning during the 2023 Amazon drought.

name: Northern Australia savannas, Aug-Sep 2011
why: August-September 2011: 73,415 harmonized hotspots in this box vs a typical 21,979 for the same months, 334% of the 2003-2022 median. Across the whole region the peak month was 325% of median. Heavy grass fuel after the very wet 2010-11 La Nina years.
